name: Device pixel ratio and zoom
plain: How many physical pixels per CSS pixel; also changes with browser zoom.
meaning: Values like 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.625, 3 reveal retina screens, Windows scaling and the person's zoom level (50% to 500%). Zoom shifts DPR so it leaks accessibility settings.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can see your screen's sharpness factor, which also shifts when you zoom
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads or you zoom.
can: Check how many real pixels sit behind each page pixel
Notice when you zoom in or out
Use the number as part of a fingerprint
cannot: See your exact screen size or model
Tell for sure whether a change came from zoom or a new screen

story.what_it_is: Tells a page how many real screen dots sit behind each page dot. It also changes when you zoom.

marketing.name: Window.devicePixelRatio
marketing.pitch: Explains how the ratio of real pixels to page pixels is used to draw sharp images and text.

story.for_you: You never see it. It is why text looks sharp on a Retina screen. When you press zoom in your browser the number changes and the page may redraw.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to draw crisp canvases and send the right image size. It also leaks your zoom level, which is one more clue to tell your browser apart from others.

use_cases.example: A browser game sizes its drawing canvas by the ratio so pixel art stays sharp on Retina and does not crush a weak phone.
A design tool redraws lines and text when you zoom the browser so they stay crisp.
A web map picks sharp or standard tiles and keeps labels readable.
A store gives a phone small high quality images and a desktop the larger ones.
A fraud check notices a login from a window whose ratio never changes, a sign of an automated browser.
A tracking script reads the ratio and zoom to help recognise the same browser across sites.

technical_bounds: Desktop DPR mixes OS scaling and browser zoom

linkedin.how: Collected as device pixel ratio. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
